teacher_walkthrough:
Pia's daily running times in minutes follow a normal distribution with mean $\mu = 10.1$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 1.3$:
$$X \sim \mathrm{N}(10.1, 1.3^2)$$

We want to find the probability that on a randomly chosen day she takes longer than 11.3 minutes:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 11.3)$$

Step 2: Relate to the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > 0.923) = 1 - \Phi(0.923)$$

Step 3: Look up $\Phi(0.923)$ in the standard normal table:
$$\Phi(0.92) = 0.8212$$
Using the differences table for 3:
$$\text{Difference for } 3 = 8 \implies \Phi(0.923) = 0.8212 + 0.0008 = 0.8220$$

Step 4: Subtract from 1:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 11.3) = 1 - 0.8220 = 0.1780$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.178$.

hints: We are given $\mathrm{P}(X > t) = 0.75$, which means $\mathrm{P}(X < t) = 0.25$.
Because the area below $t$ is $0.25 < 0.5$, $t$ lies below the mean, so the $z$-value is negative.
From the critical values table, $\Phi(0.674) = 0.75$, so $z = -0.674$.
Set up the standardisation equation $\dfrac{t - 10.1}{1.3} = -0.674$ and solve for $t$.
walkthrough:
Convert the upper-tail probability statement to a cumulative probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > t) = 0.75 \implies \mathrm{P}(X < t) = 0.25$$

Find the critical $z$-value from standard normal tables:
$$\Phi(0.674) = 0.75 \implies z = -0.674$$

Equate the standardised cutoff to $z$ and solve for $t$:
$$\dfrac{t - 10.1}{1.3} = -0.674$$
$$t - 10.1 = 1.3 \times (-0.674) = -0.8762$$
$$t = 10.1 - 0.8762 = 9.2238 \approx 9.22\text{ minutes}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
We are given that on 75% of days, Pia takes longer than $t$ minutes to run 2 km:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > t) = 0.75$$

Step 1: Determine the sign of the $z$-score.
Since $0.75 > 0.5$, the area to the right of $t$ is greater than half the distribution.
Therefore, $t$ must be below the mean $\mu = 10.1$, and the lower-tail area is:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < t) = 1 - 0.75 = 0.25$$

Step 2: Find the corresponding $z$-score.
By symmetry of the normal curve:
$$\Phi(-z) = 0.75$$
From the critical values table for the normal distribution:
$$\Phi(0.674) \approx 0.7500 \implies -z = 0.674 \implies z = -0.674$$

Step 3: Equate the standardised expression to $z$:
$$\frac{t - 10.1}{1.3} = -0.674$$

Step 4: Solve for $t$:
$$t - 10.1 = -0.674 \times 1.3 = -0.8762$$
$$t = 10.1 - 0.8762 = 9.2238$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $t = 9.22$ minutes.

hints: Check symmetry around the mean $\mu = 10.1$: $10.1 - 8.9 = 1.2$ and $11.3 - 10.1 = 1.2$.
By symmetry, the lower tail $\mathrm{P}(X < 8.9)$ equals the upper tail $\mathrm{P}(X > 11.3) = 0.178$.
Calculate the central interval probability: $\mathrm{P}(8.9 < X < 11.3) = 1 - 2(0.178) = 0.644$.
Multiply by the 90 days to estimate the expected number of days: $90 \times 0.644 = 57.96 \approx 58$ (or 57) days.
walkthrough:
Observe the symmetry of the boundaries around the mean $\mu = 10.1$:
$$10.1 - 8.9 = 1.2 = 11.3 - 10.1$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 8.9) = \mathrm{P}(X > 11.3) = 0.178$$

Calculate the central probability of running between 8.9 and 11.3 minutes:
$$\mathrm{P}(8.9 < X < 11.3) = 1 - 2 \times 0.178 = 1 - 0.356 = 0.644$$

Multiply by the 90 days to find the expected frequency:
$$\text{Expected days} = 90 \times 0.644 = 57.96 \approx 58 \text{ (or 57) days}$$
teacher_walkthrough: We want to find how many days in a 90-day period Pia is expected to take between 8.9 and 11.3 minutes to run 2 km.

Step 1: Find the probability $\mathrm{P}(8.9 < X < 11.3)$.
Notice that the boundaries are equidistant from the mean $\mu = 10.1$:
$$10.1 - 8.9 = 1.2$$
$$11.3 - 10.1 = 1.2$$
Because the normal curve is symmetrical about the mean, the two outer tails have identical probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 8.9) = \mathrm{P}(X > 11.3)$$
From part (a), $\mathrm{P}(X > 11.3) = 0.178$.
Therefore, the probability of falling in the central region is:
$$\mathrm{P}(8.9 < X < 11.3) = 1 - 2 \times \mathrm{P}(X > 11.3) = 1 - 2(0.178) = 1 - 0.356 = 0.644$$

Step 2: Calculate the expected number of days.
In a period of $n = 90$ days:
$$\text{Expected days} = n \times p = 90 \times 0.644 = 57.96$$
An integer estimate of 57 or 58 days is accepted (58 is nearest whole integer).
